newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China aluminium smelter to expand capacity in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China aluminium smelter to expand capacity in 1997.

text.p: China's Tongchuan Shining Aluminium Co plans to boost its aluminium production capacity by 25 percent to 50,000 tonnes per year in 1997, a company official said on Tuesday.
"We currently produce around 40,000 tonnes of aluminium a year, largely for sale in the domestic market," the official told Reuters by telephone from Tongchuan city in the central province of Anhui.
The official did not specify when in 1997 the smelter would launch expanded production.
The smelter had recently sought to export about 1,000 tonnes of aluminium but had been discouraged by a weak international market, the official said.

The price of aluminium in the domestic market was about 13,300 yuan to 13,500 yuan (US$1,602 to $1,626) per tonne, he said. Aluminium was quoted at $1,451 per tonne on the London Metal Exchange on Monday.
China's domestic market for aluminium is weak since the construction sector and other industries remain sluggish in the tail end of an economic slowdown following austerity measures.
"But after the winter, spring is not far behind," the official said, noting that next year's expansion of the company's production capacity was geared to a healthier market.

Plagued by energy shortages, output from Chinese aluminium smelters is expected to grow in 1996 by just 1.7 percent over 1995 production to 1.7 million tonnes, Metal Bulletin Research senior metals analyst Raju Daswani said in a recent report.
China's economy is expected to improve in the fourth quarter of 1996, compared with the third quarter, official media have said.
The fourth-quarter gross domestic product (GDP) was forecast to climb a year-on-year 10 percent to 2.340 trillion yuan ($282 billion).
Officials have said they want to curb economic growth below 10 percent this year to prevent an overheating of the economy after GDP growth of 10.2 percent in 1995.
